title: Graphene Sandwiches with Controlled Surface Functionalization for Room-Temperature TEM Imaging of Uniformly Encapsulated Solvated Proteins
content: The structural and functional complexity of proteins is significantly influenced by water, which mediates many of the non-covalent intramolecular, intermolecular, and protein-solvent interactions [1]. Understanding protein behavior in solvated conditions is therefore crucial for elucidating biological mechanisms [2] and engineering novel biointerfaces [3]. High-resolution visualization using cryogenic electron microscopy (cryo-EM) and liquid-phase electron microscopy (LP-EM) enables such observations of solvated protein structures. For both techniques, sample thinness and uniform distribution are critical for achieving high-quality imaging.
